Before enabling: write CTRLA.MODE 0x0 (external clock) or 0x1 (internal clock); choose asynchronous or synchronous with CTRLA.CMODE; choose the receive pad with CTRLA.RXPO and the transmit and clock pads with CTRLA.TXPO; set the character size in CTRLB.CHSIZE and the bit order in CTRLA.DORD; for parity, choose even or odd in CTRLB.PMODE and set CTRLA.FORM to 0x1; set the stop bits in CTRLB.SBMODE; with the internal clock, write BAUD; then enable receiver and transmitter with CTRLB.RXEN and CTRLB.TXEN. CTRLA.ENABLE enables it and CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DBGCTRL and disables it.

In both modes the shift clock comes from the baud-rate generator or from the XCK pin. CTRLA.CMODE = 1 selects synchronous and 0 asynchronous; CTRLA.MODE = 0x1 selects the internal clock and 0x0 the external. Asynchronous operation uses the 16-bit BAUD value, synchronous the 8 low bits. In synchronous mode CTRLA.MODE sets whether XCK is an input or an output; RxD is sampled on the XCK edge opposite the one that changes TxD. With CTRLA.CPOL = 0 data changes on the rising XCK edge and is sampled on the falling edge; with CPOL = 1 the reverse. With the clock on XCK (MODE = 0x0) the shift registers run straight from XCK, unsynchronized, up to the system frequency.

TxDATA and RxDATA share one address, DATA: writing loads the transmit register, reading returns the receive register. Writing DATA starts a transmission; the data moves to the shift register when it is empty and one whole frame goes out. INTFLAG.TXC sets when the frame and its stop bits are out and nothing new is waiting; DATA should be written only while INTFLAG.DRE is set. Clearing CTRLB.TXEN disables the transmitter only after pending and ongoing transmissions end. Reception starts on a valid start bit; bits are sampled at the baud rate or on XCK until the first stop bit, then the frame moves to the two-level buffer and INTFLAG.RXC sets; a second stop bit is ignored. DATA should be read only while RXC is set. Clearing CTRLB.RXEN flushes the buffer and loses any frame in progress. STATUS holds three error bits, FERR (frame), BUFOVF (overflow) and PERR (parity), each set until a one is written to it or the receiver is disabled. With CTRLA.IBON = 1 BUFOVF sets the moment the buffer overflows (empty it by reading until RXC clears); with IBON = 0 the overflow travels with the data and BUFOVF sets with RXC once the data is read. For asynchronous reception, clock recovery aligns incoming frames to the internal baud clock and data recovery samples and low-pass filters each bit.

The receiver tolerates a limited difference between the incoming bit rate and its own baud rate, which comes from reference clock instability and from the BAUD division not being exact; BAUD is chosen for the lowest error. The recommended maximum receiver error assumes receiver and transmitter share the total error equally. In asynchronous mode three middle samples decide each bit by majority vote; with CTRLA.SAMPA = 0 these are samples 7-8-9 at 16x oversampling and 3-4-5 at 8x.
CTRLA.FORM = 0x1 turns parity on. CTRLB.PMODE = 0 gives even parity (the parity bit makes the count of ones even), 1 gives odd. On reception the parity is recomputed and a mismatch sets STATUS.PERR.

RTS and CTS connect crosswise to the remote device (TXD to RXD, RXD to TXD, CTS to RTS, RTS to CTS). Available only with the internal clock (CTRLA.MODE = 1), asynchronous mode (CTRLA.CMODE = 0) and the flow-control pinout (CTRLA.TXPO = 2). RTS is driven high by the receiver while disabled or while its receive FIFO is full, telling the remote to stop after the frame in progress; RXEN sets and clears RTS after a synchronization delay, and a full FIFO sets RTS at once, holding the frame being received in the shift register until there is room. STATUS.CTS shows the CTS level; a character starts only while CTS is low, and when CTS goes high transmission stops after the frame in progress.

IrDA-compliant modulation up to 115.2 kb/s needs CTRLB.ENC = 1, asynchronous mode (CTRLA.CMODE = 0) and 16x sampling (CTRLA.SAMPR[0] = 0). Each low bit is sent as a high pulse 3/16 of a bit period wide. The decoder synchronizes its baud counter at the start of each zero pulse and accepts a pulse at least as long as RXPL.RXPL sets (RXPL = 19 means at least 20 serial engine clock cycles; with BAUD = 0xE666, 160 cycles a bit, that is 2/16 of a bit); an accepted bit passes to the receiver at mid-bit. Transmitter and receiver polarities are opposite: a zero is sent as a pulse, and an accepted pulse is received as a zero.

Needs an auto-baud frame format (CTRLA.FORM = 0x04 or 0x05), asynchronous mode and 16x sampling with fractional baud generation (CTRLA.SAMPR = 1). It follows LIN: more than 11 consecutive dominant bits at the set baud rate is a Break Field and sets INTFLAG.RXBRK; the following Sync Field must be 0x55. From the Sync start bit a counter runs for 8 bit times; its 13 high bits (the count divided by 8) become BAUD.BAUD and its 3 low bits BAUD.FP, loaded after a synchronization delay. A Sync character other than 0x55 sets STATUS.ISF and INTFLAG.ERROR and leaves the baud rate as it was. Data characters follow.

With receiver and transmitter joined, by pin configuration or outside, and both enabled, CTRLB.COLDEN checks each transmitted bit against the received one; receiving while the transmitter is idle is not a collision. On a collision the transfer is aborted, the transmit buffer flushed and the transmitter disabled (CTRLB.TXEN = 0, done after synchronization with SYNCBUSY.CTRLB set meanwhile), leaving TxD tri-stated; STATUS.COLL and INTFLAG.ERROR set, and INTFLAG.TXC sets as the buffer is empty. Software re-enables the transmitter once SYNCBUSY.CTRLB is clear.
Setting CTRLA.RXPO and CTRLA.TXPO to the same data pad loops transmit to receive at the pad, so the pin carries the signal too.

CTRLB.SFDE turns it on, in asynchronous and synchronous modes. A falling edge on RxD powers up the 8MHz internal oscillator and the USART clock so the rest of the frame can be received, if the baud rate is slow enough against the oscillator's start-up time, which varies with supply and temperature. In standby the fast start-up internal oscillator must be the GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE source. With INTENSET.RXS set the Receive Start interrupt fires at once; without it the oscillator and clock stay on for the frame and the CPU wakes only on Receive Complete, if enabled.

Two DMA requests: RX, set while the receive FIFO holds data and cleared by reading DATA; TX, set while the transmit buffer is empty and cleared by writing DATA. Seven interrupt sources (Error, Received Break, Clear to Send Input Change, Receive Start, Receive Complete, Transmit Complete, Data Register Empty) share one line, each with its INTFLAG bit enabled through INTENSET and INTENCLR. No events.

With the internal clock, CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1 keeps GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE on in all sleep modes and any interrupt can wake the device; with an external clock, RUNSTDBY = 1 lets Receive Start or Receive Complete wake it. With RUNSTDBY = 0 the internal clock stops when the transfer in progress ends and Receive Start or Transfer Complete can wake the device; an external clock is disconnected when the transfer ends and further reception is dropped. Writes to CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, CTRLB.RXEN and CTRLB.TXEN are synchronized: SYNCBUSY.SWRST, SYNCBUSY.ENABLE or SYNCBUSY.CTRLB is one meanwhile, and another synchronized access during that time causes a peripheral bus error.

SPI is a SERCOM mode: a four-wire (MISO, MOSI, SCK, SS) full-duplex link with a single-buffered transmitter and a double-buffered receiver, all four SPI modes, LSB or MSB first, 8- or 9-bit characters and DMA. A single data direction frees MISO or MOSI for another function. As master it uses the baud-rate generator (8-bit) for a serial clock up to 12MHz and can drive SS in hardware; as slave it takes a serial clock up to the system clock, can match an 8-bit address, works in all sleep modes and wakes on an SS transition.

The SPI keeps running in any sleep mode and its interrupts can wake the device. CLK_SERCOMx_APB is gated in the PM; GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE must be set up and enabled in the GCLK before use and is asynchronous to the bus clock, so some register writes need synchronization. DMA requests go to the DMAC and the interrupt to the NVIC; there are no events. It keeps running in debug halt unless DBGCTRL halts it. All writable registers can be PAC protected except INTFLAG, STATUS and DATA; protection is lifted during debug halt and never applies to an external debugger.

As master the SPI starts and controls every transaction. DATA can take the next character while one is being sent, and received characters move into a two-level buffer. A transaction is one or more characters of 8 or 9 bits: the master pulls the slave's SS low, both load their shift registers, the master drives SCK, data moves master to slave on MOSI and slave to master on MISO, one character in for each character out, and the master ends the transaction by taking SS high.

CTRLA (except ENABLE and SWRST), CTRLB (except RXEN), BAUD and ADDR can be written only while the SPI is disabled; writes while it is enabled or being enabled are dropped, and writes while it is being disabled take effect once disabled. Before enabling: write CTRLA.MODE 0x2 (slave) or 0x3 (master); choose the transfer mode with CTRLA.CPOL and CTRLA.CPHA; the transaction format with CTRLA.FORM; the receive pad with CTRLA.DIPO; the transmit, SS and SCK pads with CTRLA.DOPO; the character size with CTRLB.CHSIZE; the bit order with CTRLA.DORD; as master, write BAUD, and set CTRLB.MSSEN for hardware SS; enable the receiver with CTRLB.RXEN. CTRLA.ENABLE enables it and CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DBGCTRL and disables it.

As master (CTRLA.MODE = 0x3) SCK comes from the baud-rate generator in synchronous mode using the 8-bit BAUD value. As slave (CTRLA.MODE = 0x2) the external master's SCK clocks the shift register directly. TxDATA and RxDATA share the address DATA: a write goes to transmit, a read returns received data.

With CTRLB.MSSEN = 0 the SS line may be any GPIO, set as an output, and software drives it low before the transaction and high after; with MSSEN = 1 hardware drives it. A character written to DATA moves to the shift register when that is empty, which sets INTFLAG.DRE so the next can be written. With the receiver enabled, each received character moves to the two-level buffer in the clock cycle its last bit arrives and sets INTFLAG.RXC. INTFLAG.TXC sets when the last character is out and DATA holds nothing new.

While SS is high the slave is idle with MISO tri-stated; DATA may be written whenever INTFLAG.DRE is set. With SS low and SCK running it samples and shifts by the set mode; DRE sets when TxDATA moves to the shift register, each received character enters the two-level buffer on its last bit and sets RXC, and TXC sets when the master takes SS high. A value written to DATA is ready for loading only after as many as three SCK cycles, and it loads at the next character boundary, so the first character of a transaction is not DATA unless preloading is used. In a multi-character transaction, DATA must be written with at least three SCK cycles of the current character left, or the previous received character is sent again. DRE sets three CLK_SERCOM_APB cycles after DATA empties.

One error bit, STATUS.BUFOVF, set until a one is written to it or the receiver is disabled. With CTRLA.IBON = 1 it sets the moment the buffer overflows (empty it by reading until RXC clears); with IBON = 0 the overflow travels with the data, and once the data is read BUFOVF and INTFLAG.ERROR set with RXC and RxDATA reads zero.

As slave (CTRLA.MODE = 0x2) with CTRLA.FORM = 0x2 the first character of each transaction is checked against the address logic. On a match RXC sets, MISO is enabled and the transaction proceeds, and a match can wake the device from sleep; without a match the whole transaction is ignored. With 9-bit characters only the lower 8 bits are compared with ADDR.

At the start of a transaction a slave first sends what is in its shift register: its reset value after a reset, otherwise the last character of the previous transaction. With CTRLB.PLOADEN set, one character written to DATA while the synchronized SS is high is preloaded into the shift register, so no dummy character goes out; a further character written before SS falls waits in DATA. Enough time must be left between SS falling and the first SCK sampling edge for SS to be synchronized and for the MISO set-up time.

With CTRLB.MSSEN = 0 a master can select several parallel slaves, each through its own GPIO SS line; the one selected drives the shared tri-state MISO. Slaves can also be chained in series on one common SS, the master shifting n characters for n slaves; that SS is driven by hardware or by software according to MSSEN.

operation.topic: SPI loop-back, hardware SS and SS low detection
operation.text: Setting CTRLA.DIPO and CTRLA.DOPO to the same data pad loops transmit to receive at the pad, so the pin carries the signal too. With CTRLB.MSSEN = 1 a master drives one SS in hardware: low at least one baud cycle before the transfer and at least one after, and high at least one baud cycle between back-to-back frames; each of these intervals is 1 to 2 baud cycles depending on the transfer mode. As slave with CTRLB.SSDE = 1 a falling SS sets INTFLAG.SSL and can wake the device.

Two DMA requests: RX, set while the receive FIFO holds data and cleared by reading DATA; TX, set while the transmit buffer is empty and cleared by writing DATA. Five interrupt sources (Error, Slave Select Low, Receive Complete, Transmit Complete, Data Register Empty) share one line, each with its INTFLAG bit enabled through INTENSET and INTENCLR. No events.

As master the generic clock keeps running in idle sleep; with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1 GCLK_SERCOM_CORE also runs in standby, and with RUNSTDBY = 0 it stops when the transaction in progress ends; either way any interrupt can wake the device. As slave, RUNSTDBY = 1 lets Receive Complete wake the device, and with RUNSTDBY = 0 all reception, including the transaction in progress, is dropped. Writes to CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE and CTRLB.RXEN are synchronized (SYNCBUSY.SWRST, SYNCBUSY.ENABLE, SYNCBUSY.CTRLB), CTRLB.RXEN with its own behaviour; another synchronized access meanwhile causes a peripheral bus error.

I2C is a SERCOM mode, master or slave, compatible with I2C, SMBus and PMBus, with DMA. It supports 100kHz and 400kHz, and 1MHz at low system clock frequencies; its outputs are slew-rate limited and its inputs filtered. As slave it works in all sleep modes, wakes on an address match, and matches in hardware 7-bit and 10-bit addresses: a unique address and/or the 7-bit general call address, an address range, or two unique addresses (usable with DMA). The master uses the baud-rate generator; the slave uses the address match logic. Master and slave each hold one shift register plus single transmit and receive buffers.

The I2C keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock source runs, and its interrupts can wake the device. CLK_SERCOMx_APB is on by default and gated in the PM. GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE is needed as master; GCLK_SERCOM_SLOW is needed only for some functions (the SMBus time-outs); both are set up and enabled in the GCLK before use and are asynchronous to the bus clock. DMA requests go to the DMAC and the interrupt to the NVIC; there are no events. It keeps running in debug halt unless DBGCTRL halts it. All writable registers can be PAC protected except INTFLAG, STATUS, ADDR and DATA; protection never applies to an external debugger.

Two lines: SDA carries packets and SCL the bus clock. The master sends a start condition, a 7-bit address and a read/write bit (read is 1, write 0); the addressed slave acknowledges (ACK is a low bit, NACK high) and data packets follow, each 8 data bits and an acknowledge bit. After a NACK from either side the master ends with a stop condition or sends a repeated start to continue.

CTRLA (except ENABLE and SWRST), CTRLB (except ACKACT and CMD), BAUD and, as slave, ADDR can be written only while the I2C is disabled; writes while it is enabled or being enabled are dropped, and writes while it is being disabled take effect once disabled. Before enabling: write CTRLA.MODE 0x4 (slave) or 0x5 (master); optionally turn on CTRLA.LOWTOUT (SCL held-low time-out), set the SDA hold time (CTRLA.SDAHOLD) and enable smart mode (CTRLB.SMEN); as master, optionally set the inactive bus time-out (CTRLA.INACTOUT); as slave choose the address match mode (CTRLB.AMODE) and write ADDR.ADDR and ADDR.ADDRMASK; as master write BAUD. CTRLA.ENABLE enables it and CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DBGCTRL and disables it.

Start and stop detectors and a bit counter follow the bus in every sleep mode; STATUS.BUSSTATE reports the state while the master is enabled: UNKNOWN (0b00), IDLE (0b01), OWNER (0b10), BUSY (0b11). After enabling the state is UNKNOWN; software can force IDLE by writing BUSSTATE, and otherwise a stop condition, or an inactive bus time-out if enabled, makes it IDLE; once known it never returns to UNKNOWN. From IDLE, a start by another master makes it BUSY until a stop (or an SMBus inactive time-out) returns it to IDLE. Writing ADDR.ADDR in IDLE issues a start and enters OWNER; a stop after an uncontested transaction returns to IDLE, while a collision means arbitration lost and BUSY until a stop. A repeated start changes the state only if arbitration is lost while sending it.

In Standard, Fast and Fast-mode Plus transfers, SCL low and high times come from BAUD, and rise and fall times from the bus. Because the bus is wired-AND, TFALL counts as part of TLOW, and TRISE lasts until a high level is seen. TLOW, TSU;STO (stop set-up), TBUF (idle time from a stop to the next start), THD;STA ((repeated) start hold) and TSU;STA (repeated start set-up) are timed with the SCL low count, BAUD.BAUDLOW when non-zero, else BAUD.BAUD; THIGH uses BAUD.BAUD. TRISE depends on the bus impedance, and TFALL on bus impedance and the open-drain sink limit, and can usually be taken as zero. For Fast-mode Plus the nominal SCL high to low ratio is 1 to 2. For High-speed mode there is no SCL synchronization: SCL comes from the GCLK and HSBAUD (and HSBAUDLOW), with a nominal high to low ratio of 1 to 2. In every case at least one of BAUD.BAUD and BAUD.BAUDLOW is set above zero.

The master is byte-oriented and interrupt-driven, handling most events itself; auto-triggered operations and smart mode (CTRLA.SMEN) cut driver code. With CTRLA.SCLSM = 0 the clock is held low either side of the ACK bit; with SCLSM = 1 interrupts come only after the ACK bit, for use when DATA need not be checked before acknowledging. High-speed mode needs SCLSM = 1.

A transaction begins when ADDR.ADDR is written with the target address plus direction bit: the master waits for an idle bus, issues a start and sends the address. Then one of four cases. (1) Arbitration lost or bus error: INTFLAG.MB and STATUS.ARBLOST set (and STATUS.BUSERR for a bus error), SDA output is disabled and SCL released, and the master stays off the bus until it is idle; clearing the interrupt flag is enough, as the other flags clear on the next ADDR.ADDR write. STATUS.RXNACK always holds the last acknowledge received. (2) No ACK: MB and RXNACK set and the clock is held; the next step is a stop (recommended) or a repeated start resending the address; the slave may be busy, asleep, absent or faulty, or the address wrong, and under SMBus a slave must ACK its address. (3) Write acknowledged: MB sets, RXNACK clears, the clock is held; continue by writing DATA.DATA, by writing ADDR.ADDR (a repeated start is inserted) or by issuing a stop. (4) Read acknowledged: the master receives the first byte, then INTFLAG.SB sets, RXNACK clears and the clock is held; continue by acknowledging and reading on (automatic on reading DATA.DATA in smart mode), by sending a new address or by a stop. In smart mode an ACK or NACK, chosen by CTRLB.ACKACT, is sent automatically for the last two choices.

After a write address is acknowledged (MB set), writing DATA.DATA sends a byte while the master watches for collisions; a collision loses arbitration and sets STATUS.ARBLOST, a success receives the slave's ACK and clears RXNACK, and MB sets either way, so ARBLOST is best tested first in the MB interrupt, address and data alike. RXNACK must be checked after each byte, and no further byte may be sent after a NACK. On reading with SCLSM = 0, SB set means one byte has arrived and the master must send ACK or NACK; arbitration can be lost while sending a NACK, in which case MB sets instead of SB. With SCLSM = 1, SB set means one byte has arrived and ACKACT has been sent; ACKACT is then set for the next acknowledge and the transfer continues by reading DATA and, outside smart mode, issuing a command.

High-speed: a master code 0000 1nnn (nnn unique to the master) is sent in Full-speed mode, written to ADDR with ADDR.HS = 0, and answered by a NACK as no slave acknowledges; arbitration happens only in this phase. On the master write interrupt that follows, the slave address is written with ADDR.HS = 1 and the master sends a repeated start and the address in High-speed mode, staying there until a stop; each repeated start again needs ADDR.HS = 1 with the address. It needs CTRLA.SPEED = 0b10 and SCLSM = 1. 10-bit: with TENBITEN = 1 writing ADDR sends two address bytes, always first with the read/write bit (ADDR.ADDR[0]) at 0. A NACK on the first byte raises the write interrupt with the NACK bit set; otherwise the write interrupt comes after the second byte. A read then needs a repeated start and the first byte again with read/write = 1. So, for a 10-bit read: write the 10-bit address to ADDR.ADDR[10:1] with ADDR.TENBITEN = 1 and ADDR.ADDR[0] = 0; on the master write interrupt write ADDR[7:0] = 11110 address[9:8] 1 with TENBITEN cleared; then transfer data.

The slave is byte-oriented and interrupt-driven, with auto-triggered operations and smart mode (CTRLA.SMEN). With CTRLA.SCLSM = 0 the clock is held low either side of the ACK bit; with SCLSM = 1 interrupts come only after the ACK bit: for a master read the address and data interrupts come together after the address acknowledge, and for a master write the first data interrupt comes after the first byte is received and acknowledged. High-speed mode needs SCLSM = 1.

After a start, the address packet is checked by the match logic; without a match the slave waits for the next start. On a match INTFLAG.AMATCH sets (with SCLSM = 1 the CTRLB.ACKACT response is sent first, automatically) and SCL is held low until AMATCH is cleared, giving software unlimited time. STATUS.DIR, updated only on a valid address, gives the direction. STATUS.COLL set means the last packet addressed to this slave collided; a collision releases SDA and SCL without telling software, so the next AMATCH is the first sign; collisions follow the SMBus Address Resolution Protocol. With SCLSM = 0: for a master read (DIR = 1) SCL is held and, after an ACK, INTFLAG.DRDY sets asking for data; for a master write (DIR = 0) SCL is held and, after an ACK, the slave waits for data, a repeated start or a stop; after a NACK it waits for a new start and address. The command CTRLB.CMD = 3 acknowledges for either direction, and writing a one to AMATCH also sends the ACKACT response.

With SCLSM = 0, after its address the slave either waits for a byte or starts sending by writing DATA.DATA. Each byte received or sent sets INTFLAG.DRDY; a received byte is then acknowledged by CTRLB.ACKACT. Received: DRDY sets and SCL is held low for software. Sent: DRDY sets on completion; after a NACK the slave must release SDA and expect a stop or repeated start. A stop sets INTFLAG.PREC and returns the slave to idle. In High-speed mode (CTRLA.SPEED = 0x2, SCLSM = 1) the slave switches between Full-speed and High-speed by itself: a start, a master code and a NACK switch it to High-speed and set STATUS.HS until a stop.

operation.topic: I2C slave 10-bit addressing and PMBus group command
operation.text: With ADDR.TENBITEN = 1 the two address bytes after a start are matched against the 10-bit address; the first byte is always acknowledged and the second raises the address interrupt. A write is followed by data bytes; a read by a repeated start and 11110 ADDR[9:8] 1, which raises a second address interrupt with DIR set, the slave matching on it because it was just addressed. With CTRLB.GCMD set and 7-bit addressing, a STOP interrupt follows any stop that ends a stretch in which this slave was addressed. This serves the PMBus group command, which sends commands to several devices in one transmission ending in a single stop, at which every addressed slave starts executing its command.

Three hardware SCL low time-outs, timed by GCLK_SERCOM_SLOW, which must come from a 32kHz oscillator: TTIMEOUT, a single SCL low period of 25-35 ms (CTRLA.LOWTOUTEN); TLOW:SEXT, a cumulative slave clock-low extension of 25 ms from start to stop of one message (CTRLA.SEXTTOEN); TLOW:MEXT, a cumulative master clock-low extension of 10 ms inside a single byte, counted from start, ACK or ACK to the next ACK or stop (CTRLA.MEXTTOEN). An SMBus-compatible SDA hold time is also available.

operation.topic: I2C smart mode, 4-wire mode and quick command
operation.text: Smart mode makes a read of DATA.DATA send the ACK or NACK set in CTRLB.ACKACT. CTRLA.PINOUT selects 4-wire mode for master or slave: the internal I2C tri-state drivers are bypassed, SCL and SDA outputs and inputs use separate pads, so joining an I2C bus takes an outside tri-state driver that meets I2C. CTRLB.QCEN enables quick command: the interrupt flag sets as soon as the slave acknowledges the address, and software then issues a stop or repeated start through CTRLB.CMD or ADDR.ADDR.

DMA needs smart mode (CTRLB.SMEN). Slave: an address match raises the address interrupt, and after it is served data moves by DMA; RX rises when a byte from a master write arrives and falls on reading DATA; TX rises when a master read wants a byte and falls on writing DATA. Master: write ADDR with the address (ADDR.ADDR), the length (ADDR.LEN) and ADDR.LENEN = 1; LEN gives 0 to 255 data bytes, which DMA moves, followed by an automatic NACK (for reads) and a stop. If the slave NACKs a master write before LEN bytes, a stop is sent and STATUS.LENERR and INTFLAG.ERROR set. RX rises when a byte of a master read arrives and falls on reading DATA; TX rises when a master write wants its next byte and falls on writing DATA.

Slave interrupt sources: Error, Data Ready, Address Match, Stop Received. Master sources: Error, Slave on Bus, Master on Bus. They share one line, each with its INTFLAG bit enabled through INTENSET and INTENCLR. No events. As master GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE keeps running in idle sleep; with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1 it also runs in standby, and with RUNSTDBY = 0 it stops when the transaction in progress ends; any interrupt can wake the device. As slave, RUNSTDBY = 1 lets Address Match wake the device, and with RUNSTDBY = 0 all reception is dropped. Writes to CTRLA.SWRST (SYNCBUSY.SWRST), CTRLA.ENABLE (SYNCBUSY.ENABLE), and STATUS.BUSSTATE, and as master ADDR.ADDR and DATA (all SYNCBUSY.SYSOP) are synchronized; another synchronized access meanwhile causes a peripheral bus error.

The timer/counter is built from a counter with prescaler, compare/capture channels and their control. It counts clock pulses or events and works as an 8-, 16- or 32-bit counter with compare/capture channels. It generates waveforms (frequency, single-slope PWM) and captures inputs (event, frequency and pulse-width capture), takes one input event, and gives interrupts and output events on counter overflow/underflow and on compare match or capture.

The TC keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock source runs; its interrupts can wake the device and its events can start actions without waking it. CLK_TCx_APB is gated in the PM. From TC1 on, instances form even/odd pairs, and each pair shares one generic clock GCLK_TCx, so the two cannot use different clocks; GCLK_TCx is asynchronous to the bus clock, so some register accesses need synchronization. The interrupt goes to the NVIC and events are set up in the EVSYS. In debug halt the TC stops unless DBGCTRL keeps it running. All writable registers can be PAC protected except INTFLAG, STATUS, READREQ, COUNT, PER and CCx; protection is lifted during debug halt and never applies to an external debugger.

The counter counts events from the EVSYS or pulses of GCLK_TCx through the prescaler. Its value goes to the compare/capture channels, which compare it with set values or capture it on an event. The 8-, 16- or 32-bit mode sets the counter range, which with the clock sets the longest time and the resolution. It counts up or down; by default it runs continuously upward, wrapping to zero at the top value. In compare mode a match with CCx can toggle output pins, for frequency and PWM generation; capture mode measures period and pulse width.

CTRLA (except RUNSTDBY, ENABLE and SWRST) and EVCTRL.EVACT can be written only while the TC is disabled; the protected CTRLA bits may be written together with CTRLA.ENABLE = 1 but not with ENABLE = 0. Before enabling: enable CLK_TCx_APB; choose 8, 16 (default) or 32 bits in CTRLA.MODE; choose a waveform mode in CTRLA.WAVEGEN; optionally a prescaler in CTRLA.PRESCALER and, if used, a PRESYNC mode in CTRLA.PRESYNC; one-shot with CTRLBSET.ONESHOT; count down from the top with CTRLBSET.DIR; enable capture channels in CTRLC.CPTEN; invert outputs in CTRLC.INVEN. CTRLA.ENABLE enables it; CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DBGCTRL and disables it, and the TC should be disabled before a reset to avoid undefined behaviour.

GCLK_TC feeds a prescaler giving divisions from 1 to 1/1024 (the full list is in CTRLA.PRESCALER); it counts to the chosen value and then toggles its output. Above one, CTRLA.PRESYNC chooses whether on overflow or underflow the prescaler resets to zero or keeps counting, and whether the counter wraps on the next GCLK_TC pulse or the next prescaled pulse (CLK_TC_CNT). Counted events bypass the prescaler.

COUNT8 has its own period register PER, usable as the top value for waveforms. COUNT16 is the default and has no period register. COUNT32 pairs two 16-bit TCs: the even-numbered one is master and the odd-numbered one slave (STATUS.SLAVE set); the slave's registers do not reflect the 32-bit counter, writing them does not affect it, and normal access to the slave's COUNT and CCx is not allowed.

Counting up, the counter wraps to zero on the cycle after the top value; counting down, it wraps to the top value after zero; in one-shot mode it stops after a wrap. CTRLBSET.DIR = 1 counts down and CTRLBCLR.DIR = 1 counts up. Reaching top or zero sets INTFLAG.OVF, and with EVCTRL.OVFEO = 1 also gives an event. COUNT can be read or written; it is zero at start unless written or reloaded at the top value after stopping while counting down. The stop command (CTRLBSET.CMD) keeps the count, clears all waveforms, stops counting and sets STATUS.STOP. A retrigger, by command (CTRLBSET.CMD) or event action (EVCTRL.EVACT), wraps a running counter to top or zero by direction and restarts a stopped one from COUNT; with the retrigger event action enabled, enabling the TC does not start it, the next event does and each later event restarts it. The count event action steps the counter up or down by CTRLBSET.DIR on each event. With the start event action, enabling the TC waits for the next event or software retrigger; events while running have no effect.

In compare mode the counter is compared continuously with each CCx. A waveform reaches its pin after choosing a waveform mode, optionally inverting it with CTRLC.INVx, and enabling the PORT multiplexer. A match sets INTFLAG.MCx on the next rising edge of CLK_TC_CNT, with an interrupt and/or event if INTENSET.MCx and/or EVCTRL.MCEOx is set. CTRLA.WAVEGEN chooses one of four modes, which also limit the top value: normal frequency (NFRQ), match frequency (MFRQ), normal PWM (NPWM) and match PWM (MPWM). In NFRQ and NPWM the top is PER in 8-bit mode (changed by writing PER) and the counter maximum in 16- and 32-bit modes. NFRQ toggles WO[x] and sets the channel flag at each CCx match. MFRQ uses CC0 as the top and toggles WO[0] at every overflow/underflow. In PWM the CCx set the duty cycle: counting up, WO[x] is set at start or at the top match and cleared at the CCx match; counting down, cleared at start or top and set at the CCx match. In MPWM CC0 is the top and WO[0] gives a negative pulse at every overflow/underflow.

The top value may be changed while running. Counting down, a new top written when the count is near zero can be missed through synchronization delay, so the counter reloads the old top and counts one extra cycle before using the new one. Counting up, a new top lower than the old one is missed if the count is already above it, and the counter runs on to its maximum value.

Capture needs the TC event input on (EVCTRL.TCEI) and the channels enabled in CTRLC.CPTENx. Event capture: any EVSYS event is timestamped into a channel; all channels share one event line, so only one should be enabled at a time. If a capture arrives while the capture flag is still set there is nowhere to keep it and INTFLAG.ERR sets. Period and pulse-width capture: EVCTRL.EVACT = PPW captures the period T into CC0 and the pulse width tp into CC1; PWP captures tp into CC0 and T into CC1; the two captures fall on opposite edges of the input, and the counter restarts on one of them, the falling edge when EVCTRL.TCINV = 1. The captured event must be asynchronous. Writing CTRLC.CPTEN = 0x3 enables both CC0 and CC1; if only one figure is needed the other channel is free. Capture overflow sets INTFLAG.ERR.

With one-shot on (CTRLBSET.ONESHOT = 1; CTRLBCLR.ONESHOT = 1 turns it off) the counter stops at the next overflow or underflow, STATUS.STOP sets and the waveform outputs go to zero. A retrigger command, retrigger event or start event restarts it, and STATUS.STOP clears.

Interrupt sources: overflow/underflow (OVF), the compare or capture channels, capture overflow error (ERR) and synchronization ready (SYNCRDY), on one shared line, each with its INTFLAG bit enabled through INTENSET and INTENCLR. Output events: overflow/underflow (OVF) and match or capture (MC), each enabled in EVCTRL. Event actions chosen in EVCTRL.EVACT: start, retrigger, count up or down (by direction), capture event, capture period, capture pulse width; EVCTRL.TCEI enables the input event.

The TC can work in any sleep mode; in standby it needs CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1. It can wake the device by interrupt from any sleep mode or act through the EVSYS. Accesses that cross from CLK_TCx_APB to GCLK_TCx set STATUS.SYNCBUSY until done, and INTFLAG.SYNCRDY can signal the end; another synchronized access meanwhile stalls the bus (it completes, but the CPU waits and interrupts stay pending). Synchronized on write: CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, CTRLC, COUNT, PERIOD and CCx. Synchronized on read: CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, CTRLC, COUNT, PERIOD and CCx.

A 12-bit analog-to-digital converter of up to 350ksps (350,000 samples per second), also set for 8- or 10-bit results to shorten conversion. Inputs are single-ended or differential, up to 32 analog inputs (25 positive and 10 negative, internal and external), including five internal ones: the bandgap, the temperature sensor, the scaled core supply and the scaled I/O supply. A gain stage gives 1/2x to 16x. Conversions are single, continuous or pin-scan, started by software or by an event (one event input) for exact timing. Results are signed or unsigned, left- or right-adjusted. It has a window monitor on a selectable channel, internal and external references chosen by four bits, hardware gain and offset compensation, averaging and oversampling with decimation up to a 16-bit result, and a selectable sampling time. Conversion range: Vref from 1v to VDDANA - 0.6V; ADCx * GAIN from 0V to -Vref.

The ADC keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock source runs; its interrupts can wake the device and its events can start actions without waking it. CLK_ADC_APB is gated in the PM. GCLK_ADC must be set up and enabled in the GCLK before use; it is asynchronous to the bus clock, so some register writes need synchronization. The interrupt goes to the NVIC and events to the EVSYS. In debug halt the ADC stops unless DBGCTRL keeps it running. All writable registers except INTFLAG can be PAC protected; protection is lifted during debug halt or an extended CPU reset and never applies to an external debugger. Pins AIN0 to AIN19 and the VREFA/VREFB pins are its analog inputs.
To reach the specified accuracy, software loads BIAS_CAL and LINEARITY_CAL, measured in production test, out of the software calibration row of NVM and writes them to CALIB.

Results are 12-bit by default; 8 or 10 bits shorten conversion and oversampling with decimation reaches 16 bits. Inputs are internal (such as the temperature sensor) or pins, converted single-ended or differential. Before enabling, the asynchronous clock source is chosen and enabled (the GCLK_ADC source is set in SYSCTRL) and the reference set up; the first conversion after a reference change must be discarded, and other settings must stay unchanged during a conversion. CTRLA.ENABLE enables the ADC; CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DBGCTRL and disables it, and the ADC must be disabled before a reset. INPUTCTRL chooses the input; the rate depends on GCLK_ADC and the prescaler. A conversion starts by writing SWTRIG.START or by an automatic trigger, or runs continuously in free-running mode, each starting at the end of the last. Each result overwrites RESULT; with more than one channel enabled it must be read when INTFLAG.RESRDY sets or INTFLAG.OVERRUN signals an overrun.
GCLK_ADC passes through a 9-bit prescaler; CTRLB.PRESCALER[2:0] picks DIV4, DIV8, DIV16, DIV32, DIV64, DIV128, DIV256 or DIV512 to give CLK_ADC.

CTRLB.RESSEL chooses 8, 10 or 12 bits; 12 after reset. Single-ended conversion, for a positive input always above the negative, gives full 12-bit positive results with the negative input on ground (internal GND, IOGND or an external ground pin, chosen in INPUTCTRL). Differential conversion, set by CTRLB.DIFFMODE, is for a positive input that can fall below the negative. Either runs single or free-running; free-running samples and converts continuously, setting INTFLAG.RESRDY after each conversion.

SWTRIG.START or the start event (EVCTRL.STARTEI) has to lead the CLK_ADC cycle that begins conversion by one or more CLK_ADC_APB cycles. Sampling takes the opening half period of CLK_ADC; SAMPCTRL.SAMPLEN lengthens sampling. Bits are then converted MSB first; in single-ended mode an amplify phase follows sampling.

AVGCTRL.SAMPLENUM sets how many consecutive results are summed. Above 16 samples the sum would overflow the 16-bit RESULT, so it is shifted right automatically. Accumulating or averaging two or more samples needs CTRLB.RESSEL written to one. Averaging sums m samples and divides by m, the division made by the automatic shift plus a further shift set in AVGCTRL.ADJRES; it improves accuracy in noise at the cost of sample rate, the effective rate falling by 1/AVGCTRL.SAMPLENUM, and INTFLAG.RESRDY sets when the average is complete.
Resolution rises from 12 bits up to 16: for n more bits, 4^n samples are accumulated and the sum shifted right by n bits, the shift being the automatic shift plus AVGCTRL.ADJRES.

WINCTRL.WINMODE[2:0] chooses the mode and WINLT and WINUT set the lower and upper thresholds, read as signed values with a differential input and unsigned otherwise. Only the bits of the resolution set in CTRLB.RESSEL count: in 8-bit mode only the lower eight bits, and in differential mode the eighth bit is the sign even if the ninth is zero. A result meeting the condition sets INTFLAG.WINMON.

Offset error is the departure of the transfer function from the ideal line at zero input; gain error is the departure of the last step's midpoint from the ideal line after offset correction. With CTRLB.CORREN = 1, OFFSETCORR is subtracted from the conversion and the difference multiplied by GAINCORR before RESULT is written. Correction adds 13 GCLK_ADC of latency to a single conversion; in free-running mode it shows only on the first conversion, as correction is shorter than the propagation delay, and later results come at the set rate.

Interrupt sources: Result Conversion Ready (RESRDY), Overrun (OVERRUN), Window Monitor (WINMON) and Synchronization Ready (SYNCRDY); RESRDY, WINMON and SYNCRDY are asynchronous and can wake the device from any sleep mode. Each has an INTFLAG bit, enabled through INTENSET and INTENCLR and cleared by writing one to it. Output events: Result Ready (RESRDY) and Window Monitor (WINMON), each enabled by its EVCTRL bit. Input event actions: start conversion (START) and flush (FLUSH), each enabled by its EVCTRL bit; with several events connected, the action follows any of them. Events are routed in the EVSYS.

In standby, CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 0 disables the ADC and powers its analog blocks off for the lowest consumption, keeping its configuration, so a start-up delay follows wake-up; RUNSTDBY = 1 keeps it running and any enabled ADC interrupt can wake the CPU, while conversions during CPU sleep can be triggered only by events. Accesses that cross from CLK_ADC_APB to GCLK_ADC set STATUS.SYNCBUSY until done, and Synchronization Ready can signal the end; another synchronized access meanwhile stalls the bus (it completes, but the CPU waits and interrupts stay pending). Synchronized on write: CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, CTRLB, SWTRIG, WINCTRL, INPUTCTRL, WINUT and WINLT. Synchronized on read: SWTRIG, INPUTCTRL and RESULT.

operation.topic: Electrical characteristics: basis of the figures
operation.text: Typical figures are for 25 °C unless a row gives another condition. Minimum and maximum figures hold over the whole operating temperature and supply range unless a row limits them.

The current consumption and wake-up figures are measured with VVDDIN = 3.3 V (rows marked VDDIN = 1.8 V run the CPU from Flash with 3 wait states). XOSC is off; XOSC32K runs on an external 32 kHz crystal and is the reference of the DFLL48M, which runs at 48 MHz and is the main clock unless a row says otherwise. CPU and AHB clocks are undivided, APBA is divided by 4, and the APBB and APBC bridges are off. Of the AHB clocks only NVMCTRL and the APBA bridge run; of the peripheral clocks only PM, SYSCTRL and RTC. I/Os are inactive with the internal pull-up on, the CPU runs from Flash with 1 wait state, the NVMCTRL cache is on and BOD33 is off. Wake-up time runs from the edge of the wake-up signal to the first instruction fetched from Flash.

Each peripheral's figure is the rise in supply current it causes, Iperiph minus Idefault. The baseline Idefault is taken with VVDDIN = 3.3 V, XOSC off, XOSC32K running on an external 32 kHz crystal, OSC8M at 8 MHz as the main clock, CPU, AHB and APBn clocks undivided, only the NVMCTRL and HPB0/1/2 bridge AHB clocks and the PM and SYSCTRL peripheral clocks running, I/Os inactive with pull-up, the CPU in IDLE0, cache on and BOD33 off. For each peripheral in turn its GCLK is set up and enabled where it has one, its bus clock unmasked and the peripheral enabled where that applies; the CPU goes to IDLE0, Iperiph is read, and the CPU is woken through the EIC (asynchronous level detection, no filter) before the peripheral, its bus clock and its GCLK are switched off again.

operation.topic: XOSC, XOSC32 and reset pins as I/O
operation.text: When the XOSC and XOSC32 pins are not used by their oscillators they act as ordinary I/O pins, with the normal I/O pin figures. The external reset pin also has the electrical figures of a normal I/O pin.
Reset is held while VDD climbs; it releases once VDD passes VPOT+. When VDD later falls, reset is asserted again as it drops through VPOT-, which sits below VPOT+.

With hysteresis off, the BOD33 asserts reset while VCC is under the single threshold VBOD and releases it when VCC is back above it. With hysteresis on, reset is asserted when VCC falls under VBOD- and released only after VCC rises above the higher threshold VBOD+.
The ADC can average a run of consecutive conversions in hardware to raise accuracy. AVGCTRL.SAMPLENUM[3:0] sets how many samples are averaged, and the averaged value appears in RESULT.

Gain and offset errors limit absolute accuracy. The ADC removes them in hardware: OFFSETCORR holds the offset correction and GAINCORR the gain correction, and both are applied to each conversion before it is written to RESULT.

Seen from outside, an ADC input is a series resistance RSAMPLE into a sampling capacitor CSAMPLE whose other plate sits at VDDIN/2. The signal source's own resistance RSOURCE adds to RSAMPLE, so the source must be able to charge CSAMPLE within the sampling time to reach full accuracy.

The sensor output is linear in temperature but also follows the internal reference, which itself drifts with temperature. Production test therefore stores a read-only Temperature Log row at address 0x00806030, holding two measured temperatures (a room and a hot insertion), the ADC result of the sensor at each, and the internal 1 V reference at each. All of it was measured with VDDIN = VDDIO = VDDANA = 3.3 V, a 1.0 MHz ADC clock, 125 ksps, 57 µs sampling time, free-running mode averaging 4 samples, each value being the mean of 10 conversions, with the internal 1.0 V reference INT1V and the sensor as input. Software reads the row to correct its temperature readings.

Each temperature is stored as an integer and a decimal part: ROOM_TEMP_VAL_INT = 25 with ROOM_TEMP_VAL_DEC = 2 means 25.2 °C, and HOT_TEMP_VAL_INT = 83 with HOT_TEMP_VAL_DEC = 3 means 83.3 °C. ROOM_ADC_VAL and HOT_ADC_VAL are the 12-bit sensor conversions at those two temperatures. ROOM_INT1V_VAL and HOT_INT1V_VAL give the internal 1 V reference at each temperature as a two's-complement offset from 1 V in 0.001 V steps: codes 0 to 127 stand for 1 V down to 0.873 V and codes -1 to -127 for 1.001 V up to 1.127 V.

In the equations, tempR and tempH are the room and hot temperatures from the log row, ADCR and ADCH the matching ADC codes (VADCR and VADCH as volts), and INT1VR and INT1VH the matching reference voltages. A sensor reading is placed on the straight line through (tempR, VADCR) and (tempH, VADCH). A first, coarse temperature assumes the reference was exactly 1 V during the reading; the reference at that coarse temperature is then interpolated between INT1VR and INT1VH and used to compute a finer temperature.
A Flash row accepts at most 8 consecutive writes; after the eighth it must be erased before it is written again.

With a crystal between XIN and XOUT, the crystal's load capacitance CL must lie inside the range in the table; the crystal's own datasheet gives its exact CL, and the two external capacitors follow from it. The same connection and equation apply to the 32 kHz oscillator. The crystal's motional branch (LM, RM, CM) and shunt capacitance CSHUNT sit between the pins, with one CLEXT from each pin to ground and CSTRAY across the pins.

In master mode the device drives SS and SCK: tMOS and tMOH place MOSI around the SCK edges, tMIS and tMIH bound MISO, and tSCK, tSCKW, tSCKR and tSCKF describe the clock. In slave mode tSSS and tSSH frame SS around the clock, tSIS and tSIH bound MOSI, tSOS sets MISO against SCK, and tSOSSS and tSOSSH set MISO against SS falling and rising. Both clock polarities (CPOL = 0 and 1) follow the same figures.

The I2C timing figures are what devices on the bus must meet. On SCL, tHIGH and tLOW are the clock phases, tR the rise time and tOF the output fall time. tSU;STA and tHD;STA bound a (repeated) START, tSU;DAT and tHD;DAT bound each data bit, tSU;STO precedes STOP, and tBUF is the idle time between a STOP and the next START.

In the read cycle the debugger's SWDIO line carries stop and park, a tri-state period, then data, data, parity and start, while the device's line returns the acknowledge between two tri-state periods. In the write cycle the debugger's line carries stop and park and then stays tri-stated until start, while the device's line carries the acknowledge, data, data and parity. THIGH and TLOW are the SWDCLK high and low phases, TOS is the SWDIO output skew against the falling SWDCLK edge, and TIS and TIH are the SWDIO input setup and hold times about the rising SWDCLK edge.

Where there is strong electromagnetic noise, three points matter most for reliable running besides general EMC practice: decoupling capacitors right at the power pins, a resistor-capacitor filter at RESET, and SWCLK pulled up. Noise should also be kept off the supply pins, the I/O pins and the crystals.
The reference circuits are needed only when the ADC uses an external reference on VREFA or VREFB; with an internal reference they can be left off.

The reset circuit goes on the RESET pin only when external reset is in use, and the push-button can be left out when no manual reset is wanted. RESET is the pin's function after power-up; it becomes a GPIO once the reset function is turned off in the External Reset Controller (EXTCTRL) register. The pin has an internal pull-up, so the external pull-up is optional; it keeps reset from being pulled low by accident. The resistor in series with the switch lets the filter capacitor discharge gently, avoiding the current surge, and the noise spike it would cause, of shorting the capacitor directly.
Unused pins need no configuration: their reset state already gives the lowest leakage current.
The device runs from internal clocks, external clocks or a mixture; one example is OSC8M as the system clock with a 32.768 kHz watch crystal on XOSC32K clocking the RTC.

XOSC32K is built for a 32.768 kHz watch crystal and for very low power, so the crystal's load capacitance and ESR, both from the crystal maker, need care; the maximum ESR for 12.5 pF crystals is in the 32 kHz crystal oscillator table. The oscillator's internal load capacitance (typical values in that table) plus the board's capacitance can be enough for a crystal of under 12.5 pF load capacitance, with no external capacitors. Adding external capacitors improves accuracy and safety factor where the crystal datasheet calls for them; the crystal datasheet gives the right load capacitance.

The load a crystal sees is made of three capacitances on each side: CLn inside the device from each oscillator pin to ground, CPn the external load capacitor, and CELn the board's parasitic capacitance. The total Ctot should equal the load capacitance the crystal maker specifies. CELn is usually small enough to ignore and otherwise depends on board material and layout. The device's own pin capacitance is in the electrical characteristics.

Programming and debugging go through the Serial Wire Debug (SWD) interface, which Atmel's SAM-ICE and JTAGICE3 and the Xplained Pro board's embedded debugger support, among third-party tools. The Xplained Pro evaluation board programs and debugs the device with no external tool. A pull-up on SWCLK is essential for reliable operation.

The JTAGICE3 does not take the Cortex 10-pin connector directly. It connects either through its squid cable, wiring each signal by hand, or through a 10-pin header laid out to match the JTAGICE3 cable.
Revision A was never sampled. The items below apply to revision B, each with its errata reference number.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, DSU: MBIST pause-on-error (14324)
operation.text: The MBIST Pause-on-Error feature does not work. Workaround: do not use it.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, DMAC: CRCDATAIN back-to-back writes (13507)
operation.text: Writing CRCDATAIN in two instructions in a row can give a wrong CRC. Workaround: put a NOP between successive writes to CRCDATAIN.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, NVMCTRL: MANW reset value (13134)
operation.text: NVM.CTRLB.MANW resets to 0, so a data write through a stray pointer into the NVM area can cause an unintended NVM write. Workaround: set MANW to 1 at start-up.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, NVMCTRL: leakage during external reset (13446)
operation.text: While external reset is held active, VDDIO draws a high leakage current. Workaround: keep external reset active as briefly as possible.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, device: BOD12 on standby exit (15513)
operation.text: On some parts the internal BOD12 comes back on too early when leaving standby sleep, which can reset the device with BOD12 as the cause. Workaround: just before entering standby, write 0x00000004 to address 0x40000838 to turn BOD12 off, and write 0x00000006 to the same address after waking to turn it back on.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, device: SYSTICK calibration value (14157)
operation.text: The SYSTICK calibration value is wrong; the right value is 0x40000000. That value is not for loading the SysTick reload register, which takes a value set by the main clock frequency and the tick period wanted. The SysTick itself is described in Arm's Cortex-M0+ documentation.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, device: read-synchronized register access with APB clock off (10416)
operation.text: Reading a read-synchronized register over APB while that APB clock is stopped and the GCLK runs freezes the device: both the CPU and the debug access port (DAP AHB-AP) hang, so debugging stops working. Workaround: do not make such reads; to recover, cycle the power or reset the device through the RESETN pin.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, device: regulator low-power mode above 85 °C (12291)
operation.text: The voltage regulator's low-power mode does not work above 85 °C. Workaround: keep the regulator in normal mode during standby sleep by setting SYSCTRL->VREG.bit.RUNSTDBY = 1.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, device: I2C slave CTRLB writes in AMATCH or DRDY handlers (13574)
operation.text: In I2C slave mode, writing CTRLB inside the AMATCH or DRDY interrupt handler can reset the state machine. Workaround: to clear CTRLB.ACKACT, write STATUS.reg = 0 and then CTRLB.reg = 0; to set it, write STATUS.reg = 0 and then CTRLB.reg = SERCOM_I2CS_CTRLB_ACKACT; with higher-priority interrupts disabled around the pair so that both writes are atomic. Otherwise write CTRLB in those handlers only to finish a transaction. When not finishing one, clear AMATCH by writing a 1 to its flag bit rather than using CTRLB.CMD; DRDY clears itself on a DATA access in smart mode and otherwise is cleared by writing a 1 to its flag bit. So a read-modify-write that sets or clears ACKACT becomes the two-write sequence above, and an address ACK/NACK done with CTRLB.CMD = 0x3 becomes: if INTFLAG.PREC is set, write SERCOM_I2CS_INTFLAG_PREC to INTFLAG, then write SERCOM_I2CS_INTFLAG_AMATCH to INTFLAG (CMD = 0x3 cleared every interrupt flag, PREC included).

operation.topic: Errata rev B, device: GCLK generators after XOSC32K failure (12164)
operation.text: If the external XOSC32K fails, neither the external reset pin nor a GCLK software reset resets the GCLK generators that use XOSC32K as their source. Workaround: cycle the power to reset them.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, DFLL48M: register write before the clock is requested (9905)
operation.text: Writing a DFLL register before the DFLL clock has been requested can freeze the device. Workaround: write 0 to DFLLCTRL.ONDEMAND before configuring the DFLL.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, DFLL48M: false out-of-bounds interrupts (10669)
operation.text: If COARSE or FINE reaches its maximum or minimum during locking, an out-of-bounds interrupt is raised even when the final locked values are not at the limit. Workaround: enable the DFLLOOB interrupt only after both DFLLLCKC and DFLLLCKF are set in the SYSCTRL INTFLAG register.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, EIC: spurious flag with filter on enable (15341)
operation.text: With the filter on (CONFIGn.FILTENx) and sensing set to low level, rising edge or both edges (CONFIGn.SENSEx), INTFLAG.EXTINT[x] for that pin can be set spuriously the moment CTRLA.ENABLE turns the EIC on. Workaround: clear INTFLAG after enabling the EIC and before enabling its interrupts.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, SERCOM: I2C SCL low extend time-outs need LOWTOUT (12003)
operation.text: The slave and master SCL low extend time-outs (CTRLA.SEXTTOEN, CTRLA.MEXTTOEN) do not work while the SCL low time-out CTRLA.LOWTOUT is off, because GCLK_SERCOM_SLOW is then not requested. Workaround: set CTRLA.LOWTOUT = 1 when using either extend time-out.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, SERCOM: USART autobaud missing stop bits (13852)
operation.text: In USART autobaud mode a missing stop bit is flagged neither as an inconsistent sync error (ISF) nor as a framing error (FERR). There is no workaround.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, SERCOM: false SPI slave select low interrupt (13369)
operation.text: Enabling the SERCOM in SPI mode with slave select low detection (CTRLB.SSDE) and CTRLB.RXEN = 1 at once can raise a false INTFLAG.SSL. Workaround: enable the SERCOM with CTRLB.RXEN = 0, then set CTRLB.RXEN = 1 in a later write.

operation.topic: Errata rev B, SERCOM: I2C master halt on debug entry (12499)
operation.text: In I2C (TWI) master mode with DBGCTRL.DBGSTOP set, a transfer should stop at once when the CPU enters debug mode; instead it stops only after the current byte completes, raising its interrupt if enabled. Workaround: keep DBGCTRL.DBGSTOP = 0 in I2C master mode while debugging.
